findings.title: Shaded Ballistae and Winter Campaign can be activated without their required Gallic recipient
findings.expected: The executor must assign the shaded Capability to a Gallic Faction. A Roman executor submitting no recipient or an explicitly Roman recipient must correct the selection before the Event commits. The selected Gallic Faction receives the actual ongoing effect.
findings.observed: On unmodified Great Revolt setup, the durable turn shape validator and public preview accept both missing and Roman recipient, and execute_decision installs the shaded Capability with no owner. This occurs with original and second-edition profiles. Card 63's production after-Harvest consumer returns None and asks no Faction. A separate source-valid Battle fixture proves ownerless Card 10 gives no post-Ambush removal request, leaving the defending Citadel alive; the same public acquisition with Belgae selected gives the request and removes the Citadel.
findings.controls: Both cards accept Belgae as recipient and record Belgae. Card 63 offers Belgae the Winter Campaign choice. Public Belgic Battle+Ambush under properly assigned Card 10 removes the exact surviving Arverni Citadel at Sequani. All before/after pool and structure checks pass; previews leave live state/RNG unchanged.
findings.cause: The two copied acquisition handlers activate first, convert an invalid recipient to None, fall back only for Gallic executors, and never require a resulting owner. Consumers correctly require an owner, so the skipped selection silently suppresses the benefit.
findings.prior_distinction: Not a repeat of fourth-audit BE4-04: shaded Germanic Horse belongs to its Gallic executor and previously could be gifted. Cards 10/63 instead require an independently selected Gallic recipient even when the executor is Roman. Original Battle/Winter Campaign human-choice repairs repaired consumers, not this acquisition validation.
findings.fixture_limits: Acquisition uses ordinary setup_scenario Great Revolt seed17 boards, selecting the audited current card without claiming a naturally sampled sequence. Ballistae follow-through uses a controlled initialized position assembled with piece helpers and the permanent Provincia Fort, an exact Sequani Citadel allegiance, one Belgic Warband plus Ambiorix, and four Revealed defending Arverni Warbands. Winter Campaign is the production consumer invoked directly at its after-Harvest boundary, not a claimed full Winter run.
findings.comparison_pattern: Typed, mandatory Event selections must be validated before committing, and stored effects must be traced to actual consumers. LoD event_choices.py:125-137 and coin-implementation-lessons.md data-shape/cross-faction sections guided the check, not the game-rule conclusion.
findings.repair_scope: Share or align recipient validation for numeric10/numeric63 shaded. Preserve allowed Gallic-to-other-Gallic gifts and NPC selection rules; reject missing/invalid human recipients rather than recording ownerless effects. Do not globally infer owners for historical unknown-provenance saves.

findings.title: Colony creates a Tribe and Ally in nonplayable map areas
findings.expected: Colony selects a playable Region under the executing Faction's Control or No Control. Its exception creates an additional Tribe circle in that Region; it does not turn a nonplayable area into a Region. Reject base Cisalpina without Gallia Togata and Ariovistus Britannia before adding any Tribe, marker or Ally.
findings.observed: From ordinary Great Revolt seed17 setup, a Roman public Event71 naming Cisalpina succeeds and creates Colony_Cisalpina, its marker and one Roman Ally despite no Gallia Togata. From ordinary Ariovistus seed17 setup, the same plan naming Britannia succeeds and creates Colony_Britannia and its Roman Ally. is_region_playable is false in both cases; durable shape validation, public mechanical preview and live execution all accept. Census and structural checks remain clean.
findings.controls: Roman Colony in Provincia succeeds in both scenarios. A real Card5 Gallia Togata followed by Roman Colony in Cisalpina succeeds legally. Each control creates exactly one matching named Tribe and Ally with clean inventory/structure.
findings.cause: The Colony handler checks only Control. Every represented map area has an empty space entry, and an empty nonplayable area reports No Control. No scenario-aware geography or faction stacking check guards marker/Tribe creation.
findings.prior_distinction: Third-audit BE3-03 fixed creating a legal Colony under scarce Ally supply; XC3-01 fixed existing dynamic Tribe consumers. This finding concerns the location of new Colony creation and reaches both base and expansion nonplayable areas. CM3-01 was ordinary Scout geography, a different execution path.
findings.fixture_limits: All main witnesses and controls start from full setup_scenario boards. The current card is selected explicitly for the probe. Both numeric71 and the geography rules are valid in the stated scenario. No forbidden off-deck numeric replacement card is used.
findings.comparison_pattern: Verify the actual selected location against current board rules, rather than equating storage presence or a generic No Control result with playability. LoD coin-implementation-lessons.md boundary/data-shape checks guided the probe.
findings.repair_scope: Validate the selected Colony Region with the state-aware geography and executor stacking rules before any new Tribe or marker is installed. Retain legal Gallia Togata access, No Control choices, and scarce-Ally creation.

findings.title: Forced Marches rejects legal Cisalpina movement after Gallia Togata
findings.expected: After Gallia Togata makes Cisalpina a playable Roman Region, Forced Marches may relocate the executor's Roman mobile pieces into or out of it. The card's sole geographic exclusion is Britannia, subject to ordinary current stacking rules.
findings.observed: On a full Great Revolt seed17 board, public Card5 correctly installs the marker and three Auxilia. A subsequent public Card32 selecting one Auxilia Cisalpina to Provincia is rejected with 'Forced Marches requires playable Regions'. A separate identical board rejects the legal reverse move from Provincia to Cisalpina. Both original and second-edition profiles fail, and the atomic rollback preserves the pieces and RNG.
findings.controls: Card32 Provincia to Sequani succeeds, moving exactly one Auxilia. Without Card5, Provincia to Cisalpina is correctly rejected. In the failing Card5 cases, the production is_region_playable helper returns true for both endpoints.
findings.cause: The handler calls get_playable_regions(scenario, state['capabilities']), while Card5 stores its map-changing state as a regional marker. The state-aware geography adapter already combines that marker with the legacy capability representation, but this Event does not call it.
findings.prior_distinction: New legal-choice failure in numeric32. Third-audit CM3-01 admitted illegal ordinary Scout into inactive Cisalpina; this is the opposite effect in a separate Event path after a real marker writer. Not a repeat of Interlude deck/Nori repairs.
findings.fixture_limits: Main witnesses are full Great Revolt scenario setups followed by an actual public Gallia Togata Event. Card order is controlled, not claimed to have arisen in a sampled game. No numeric32 claim is made in Ariovistus, whose ordinary deck replaces it with A32.
findings.comparison_pattern: Trace a legitimate writer to all consumers using the actual saved representation. LoD coin-implementation-lessons.md section B describes the same producer/consumer representation failure class.
findings.repair_scope: Use state-aware, faction-aware Region eligibility for numeric32 without widening Britannia or Gallia Togata's Roman-only constraints. Include marker-form and legacy compatibility controls.

findings.expected: Abatis acts as a Fort while its owner defends. Once ordinary Warbands are removed, the human may choose an eligible Ally instead of rolling for the marker. Diviciacus cannot absorb while the Abatis can still absorb.
findings.observed: In the Ally witness, four Roman Legions cause two halved Losses to one Aedui Warband plus an Ally and Abatis. The Warband is offered, then the engine rolls/removes Abatis without a second loss-order request and preserves the Ally. In the Diviciacus witness, replacing the Ally with Diviciacus makes the engine offer and remove Diviciacus on seed2 while leaving Abatis in place.

findings.title: Diviciacus protection evaluates unrelated opponents and omits Ariovistus Counterattack doubling
findings.expected: Apply A8.6.2 to the actual selected defender and actual possible Counterattack. Diviciacus plus one Warband may safely Battle a lone Belgic Ally regardless of ten unrelated German Warbands sharing the Region. Conversely, with one escort he may not Battle Ariovistus, who can survive the Attack and inflict two Counterattack Losses.
findings.observed: The public Aedui dispatcher returns Pass in the safe Belgic-Ally case when unrelated Germans are present, but Battle when they are absent. In a second fixture it Battles at Veneti to remove a Belgic Ally and adds the Carnutes Battle against Ariovistus. Seed 6 leaves Ariovistus alive and removes both the Aedui escort and Diviciacus. Changing only Ariovistus to his Successor leaves Diviciacus alive, as one Counterattack Loss is absorbed by the escort.
findings.cause: node_a_battle removes Diviciacus's entire Region using a max-over-all-enemies helper before selecting a target. That helper uses a raw estimate that omits Ariovistus's Counterattack multiplier. These are grouped around the same defective safety check, not counted as separate findings.

findings.title: German Battle selection uses pre-Attack Counterattack forces and omits Ariovistus attack doubling
findings.expected: Six Revealed German Warbands versus six Revealed Roman Auxilia must Battle under A8.7.1: three Attack Losses leave three Auxilia for one Counterattack Loss, so 3 > 1. Ariovistus with four Warbands versus six Auxilia is also favorable: six Attack Losses remove every Auxilia and leave zero Counterattack.
findings.observed: The public German dispatcher predicts 3 versus 3 in both cases and chooses/executes March to Veneti. A normal validated public Battle from the identical initial board produces the source-derived 3/1 or 6/0 losses with clean post-state integrity.
findings.cause: The German-specific _estimate_battle_losses calculates Counterattack using the entire starting defender stack and uses only 1/2 per German Warband plus one Leader, without Ariovistus doubling. _can_battle_in_region rejects the resulting equal estimate before any SA forecast.

findings.controls: Six Germans versus four Auxilia correctly selects Battle (3 Attack, 0 Counterattack). Six Germans versus twelve Auxilia correctly selects March (3 Attack, 4 Counterattack). All witnesses disable SA through the standard Command-only planning flag and use no saving-roll pieces among defenders, avoiding forecast-policy ambiguity.

findings.expected: Restoring the Aedui Tribe at Bibracte or Arverni Tribe at Gergovia removes what occupies that Tribe circle/City. Roman Legions and other Forces elsewhere in the containing Region remain subject to their own Interlude instructions. Roman reductions expressly exclude Legions, and a declined expedition changes no Roman Forces.

Full third-Winter resolution restores a vacant home Tribe but also sends a colocated Roman Legion to the Legions Track. Six on-map Legions become five. The matched controls with the home Tribe occupied retain all six. Census/structure checks pass before and after every case.

findings.fixture: Controlled Gallic War setup, seed21. One Roman Legion moves from Provincia to the selected home Region with the normal piece helper. One Belgic Namnetes Ally is placed legally from Available so neither vacant-home witness passes Roman victory. Home Ally removed with _unally_tribe only in defect variants. All restricted Tribe ownership and permanent Provincia Fort assertions pass. Set winter_count2/current Winter to enter third Victory Phase. Romans are human and explicitly decline Britannia expedition; other seats are NP. Other human Interlude choices use the documented raw API default policy. This is a controlled phase integration, not a claim of sampled gameplay reach.
findings.controls: Occupied home Tribe controls retain the Legion in its Region and leave six on-map Legions; vacant cases restore the same Tribe but remove the Legion. No monkeypatches or engine edits.
findings.distinct_from: Earlier Interlude choice findings fixed human selection and bookkeeping. WS4-03 removes obsolete Nori at scenario change. Neither covers the Bibracte/Gergovia Region-wide wipe. Existing test_interlude_aedui_choices:test_bibracte_is_restored_when_only_a_colony_ally_survives_in_its_region and test_interlude_arverni_choices:test_cadurci_does_not_prevent_gergovia_restoration_and_reinforcement currently assert collateral clearing; those tests need source-correct expectations, not preservation.
findings.comparator_pattern: coin-implementation-lessons.md D: per-space scope must match the actual specified object; apply independently to City/Tribe versus containing Region.
